app.name: AmberBeam
app.tagline: Dual-pane FTP and SFTP client for macOS, Windows and Linux — local and remote side by side, with the keyboard in charge.
column.name: Name
log.title: Server log
queue.title: Queue
queue.empty: Nothing waiting. Drag files into a pane, or use the transfer button.
status.keys: Tab / F6 switch side · Enter open · Backspace up · Space mark · F5 refresh
quick.title: Quick connect
quick.password.hint: Kept in memory for this session only — never written to disk. The system credential store arrives with the site manager.
quick.agent.hint: Uses whatever your running ssh-agent holds, including keys on a hardware token.
hostkey.unknown.title: Unknown server
hostkey.unknown.body: {host} has not been seen before. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server's owner gave you.
hostkey.unknown.hint: Accepting records the key in ~/.ssh/known_hosts — the same file the terminal uses.
hostkey.changed.title: The server key has changed
hostkey.changed.body: {host} answers with a different key than the one on file.
hostkey.changed.warning: This is either a reinstalled server or somebody sitting between you and it. AmberBeam cannot tell the difference. Ask the operator before you accept anything.
error.authentication-failed: The server refused the credentials for {user}.
error.key-file: {path} could not be read as a key.
error.agent: No agent answered, or it holds nothing the server accepts.
certificate.title: The server's certificate was not accepted
certificate.body: {host} sent a certificate this computer does not vouch for. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server's owner gave you.
certificate.scope: This applies to this one certificate on {host}. A different certificate asks again.
certificate.unknown-issuer: Nobody this computer trusts vouches for it — it is signed by itself or by an unknown authority.
certificate.expired: It was valid once and has expired.
certificate.not-yet-valid: It is not valid yet. One of the two clocks is wrong.
certificate.wrong-name: It was issued for a different name than {host}.
certificate.revoked: It was withdrawn by the authority that issued it. Do not accept it.
certificate.broken: Its signature does not hold. Do not accept it.
certificate.other: It was refused for a reason with no better name.
error.certificate-untrusted: {host} sent a certificate that was not accepted.
error.encryption-refused: The connection could not be encrypted.
connection.unencrypted.title: This connection carries the password and every file in the clear.
connection.exception.title: This server is trusted by a fingerprint you accepted, not by a certificate authority.
appearance.title: Appearance
language.title: Language
perm.title: Permissions
perm.recursive.warning: Every file and folder below gets these exact bits — including files that were executable and now may not be.
perm.links: Symbolic links keep their own bits: there is no way to set a link's permissions without changing what it points at instead.
delete.title: Delete
delete.recursive: This removes {count} entries in total, including everything inside the folders.
delete.truncated: More than {count} entries. Counting stopped there; the deletion would not.
delete.links.hint: Links are removed as links. What they point at stays.
error.source-changed: The source has changed since the transfer stopped. Continuing would stitch two versions together.
queue.through.hint: Between two servers the data travels through AmberBeam — down from one, up to the other. This is not FXP, where the servers would talk to each other directly.
support.star.hint: Open the repository. A star is how the next person finds it.
conflict.title: Already there
conflict.body: A file of this name is already at the target. What should happen to it?
conflict.resume.hint: Continuing appends to what is there. AmberBeam cannot tell whether that half came from this same file, so this one is on you.
conflict.for-all: Do the same for the other {count} waiting
settings.title: Settings
settings.concurrency.hint: Empty lets the protocol decide: eight for SFTP, because OpenSSH allows ten, and four for FTP, because shared hosters often allow fewer. A server that refuses more says so, and AmberBeam asks for fewer by itself.
settings.retries.hint: The pauses grow: one second, two, four, eight, sixteen. After that the job is held rather than dropped — its offset is worth more than the attempt.
settings.temporary-name.hint: A file arrives as name.ampart and is renamed once it is whole, so a half file never looks finished. Only where renaming is dependable — locally and over SFTP, not over FTP.
settings.keep-permissions.hint: Off by default: bits that made sense on one machine often make a mess on another.
settings.per-connection: A connection can carry its own values; these apply where it says nothing.
queue.lowered: The server refused more connections. Running {allowed} at a time now; raise it again in the settings if you disagree.
queue.clear.hint: Remove the jobs that are finished or skipped
queue.clear-all.hint: Empty the queue, stopping what is running
queue.reveal: Double click opens the folder this is going to
update.hint: Version {version} has been released. Opens the release notes.
settings.check-updates.hint: Asks GitHub for the newest release, once shortly after starting. Nothing about you is sent — no version, no identifier, no count. It is the only request AmberBeam makes on its own.
protocol.ftp.warning: Plain FTP sends the password and every file in the clear. Use it only where nothing else is possible.
quick.temporary-name.ftp: Not used over FTP: renaming at the end needs a right many accounts lack, and a transfer that finishes and then fails to rename leaves nothing usable behind.
sites.title: Servers
sites.empty: No entries yet. The button above makes one, or import a list from another program.
sites.pick: Pick an entry on the left, or make a new one.
sites.name: Name
sites.remember.hint: Kept in this computer's credential store, never in the site file. Turning this off deletes it.
sites.open.title: Open {name}
sites.open.body: Which side should it be opened on?
sites.password.title: Password for {name}
sites.password.body: This entry has no password stored. It is used for this connection only and kept nowhere.
import.source.sites-dat: Sites.dat of an older Windows client
import.source.sites-xml: .ftp site export of an older Windows client
import.warning.master-password: This file is protected by a master password. The servers can be read, the passwords cannot.
import.warning.some-passwords: Some passwords could not be read. Those entries arrive without one rather than with a wrong one.
import.warning.cleartext: This file holds every password in plain text. AmberBeam moves them into the credential store; the file itself is worth deleting afterwards.
import.title: Import servers
import.body: Files found in the usual places. Pick one to see what is in it — nothing is written before you say so.
import.none: Nothing found in the usual places. Drag a file onto this window.
import.drop: Or drag a file onto this window: sitemanager.xml, WinSCP.ini, wcx_ftp.ini, Sites.dat, an .ftp export, or an SSH config.
import.take-passwords.hint: They are only obscured in the source file, not encrypted. AmberBeam reads them and puts them in this computer's credential store, never in a file of its own.
